task.description:
Closing gate on WF03-ISS0209-20260821. DOC-UPDATER resolved ISS-0209 by declaring what `result.git_evidence.commit_sha_list` covers and structurally cannot cover, in a new subsection of `HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` section 2, leaving the sha write-back OPTIONAL rather than promoting it to a protocol step. Its report is `result` in `handoffs/WF03-ISS0209-20260821/step-03-commit-sha-list-scope.json`; read it there and re-derive rather than reading it back. Diff is `git show 12f8f4c` (docs), `389eb0b` (a boundary-sha write-back) and `483726a` (handoff). All local, none pushed.

You are the only gate on this run: no SECURITY-REVIEWER step (no tenant-data path, no code), no test step (no code under test), no human backstop. A PASS releases the queue task.

SCOPE OF `result.issues` ON THIS DISPATCH -- READ THIS BEFORE YOU START, IT IS A DELIBERATE CHANGE. Report a MINOR only for a DEFECT in the artefact under review: something that fails an acceptance criterion, contradicts another document, states a checkable claim that is false, or would mislead a later agent acting on it. Do NOT report stylistic preferences, wording improvements, or refinements to adjacent text that is not in this run's scope. Earlier dispatches this session invited exactly that, and the result was three consecutive runs each generated by the previous run's gate while the requirement backlog went untouched. ORCH owns that mistake -- it was in the dispatch text, not in the gates' judgement. Your verdict against the nine acceptance criteria is the deliverable. An empty `result.issues` on a clean artefact is the expected outcome, not a sign you looked too lightly.

RE-DERIVE. Each item names what you must run or open yourself:

1. THE 57% DEAD-SHA MEASUREMENT IS THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM AND IT IS NOW QUOTED IN A PROTOCOL DOC. The step reports 610 files, 276 non-empty, 261 empty, 73 without the key, 502 shas recorded, and 284 of those (57%) unresolvable via `git cat-file -t`. Re-derive it. The corpus has grown by this handoff, so expect small drift in the file counts and reconcile it; the sha figures should be stable. If the unresolvable fraction is materially different from 57%, the subsection's central factual claim is wrong and that is a FAIL.

2. THE MECHANISM BEHIND THAT NUMBER, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT ACTIONABLE RATHER THAN ALARMING. The subsection attributes the dead shas to `GIT_MERGE.md` step 5 (`git rebase origin/main`) and step 8 (`gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`). Verify both steps say what is claimed by opening `GIT_MERGE.md`, and satisfy yourself the mechanism actually explains the number -- a rebase rewrites shas and a squash discards branch commits. The step cites WF02-REQ042 as a worked case (recorded `c1a4c2e...` gone, work landed as `84a0dab ... (#123)`); check that one yourself.

3. THE REGRESS REFUTATION. The issue ORCH filed asserted that a write-back commit cannot record itself, so the regress never terminates. The step refutes this: all 21 write-back commits record exactly their immediate predecessor and stop, and none is itself recorded anywhere in the corpus. Re-derive the refutation -- it matters because ORCH's own issue text was wrong, and a protocol subsection now says so. Confirm the count and the depth-1 termination, and confirm the reported false positive really is one.

4. THE RULING ITSELF. Read the new subsection. Does it state a purpose the field still HAS (rather than leaving it decorative), state concretely what it cannot contain, and tell a reader what an empty list and a non-empty list each do and do not mean? Criterion 3 turns on the field keeping a stated purpose; criterion 1 on a reader being able to tell structural incompleteness from careless filling. Judge both against the text, not the summary.

5. ONE CANONICAL STATEMENT, AND THE FENCE AROUND SECTION 1.2. The ruling must live in one place with pointers elsewhere. Confirm `GIT_MERGE.md` step 8's addition is a pointer and not a second copy. Confirm from `git show 12f8f4c` that section 1.2 is untouched -- ISS-0206 and ISS-0208 are both still open against it and this run must not have taken their work.

6. THE BOUNDARY AND THE NO-BACKFILL RULE. The ruling is commit-scoped at `12f8f4c` per section 4.1(b) precedent. Confirm that commit exists and is the one carrying the subsection, that the 276 existing non-empty files are not backfilled, and that no historical handoff file appears in any of the three commits. Note `389eb0b` is itself a write-back that wrote `12f8f4c`'s sha into the new text -- confirm it did only that.

7. BOOKKEEPING. Both JSON files in this run's directory parse under `json.loads`. `result.status` on the step-03 handoff is one of the legal five. `handoffs/orchestrator.log` and `handoffs/registry.json` are ORCH's, deliberately uncommitted, not yours to touch -- confirm `git diff --numstat` shows 0 deletions on both and leave them alone.

VERDICT: PASS or FAIL against the nine acceptance criteria on the Step 03 handoff plus the items above. A FAIL names each failed criterion and the specific gap, per section 2's validator-fail example. Commit your own handoff file. Do not write `registry.json` or `orchestrator.log`, and do not edit `docs/` unless you are making a correction to avoid a FAIL, in which case say so explicitly; you are a gate, not a producer.

result.summary:
GATE VERDICT: PASS. All nine acceptance criteria met. All seven numbered checks re-derived first-hand from the repository; nothing was taken from the step-03 report. Three quoted figures came back slightly off and are filed as MINORs below, none of them material to the ruling, and the two load-bearing claims (checks 1 and 3) both hold.

CHECK 1 -- CORPUS MEASUREMENT, RE-DERIVED. Own script, python 3.12 from the repo root: walk `handoffs/`.rglob('*.json') excluding registry.json, json.loads each, read result.git_evidence.commit_sha_list, then `git cat-file -t` every recorded sha. MY NUMBERS NOW: 611 files, 0 unparseable; 277 non-empty, 261 empty, 73 without the key; 504 shas recorded; 293 unresolvable = 58.1%. DRIFT RECONCILES EXACTLY against the step's 610/276/261/73/502. +1 file is this gate handoff (empty list). The step-03 handoff flipped empty -> non-empty when 483726a committed it, so non-empty +1 and empty -1, and the new empty gate handoff puts empty back at 261: 277+261+73 = 611. Its two shas (12f8f4c, 389eb0b) are the +2, and both resolve. So at the step's own measurement moment the unresolvable count was 293 of 502 = 58.4%, not the 284 = 57% it reported. THE 9-SHA DELTA IS FULLY EXPLAINED AND IS A CLASSIFICATION ERROR, NOT DRIFT: exactly 9 recorded strings are not sha-shaped (fail `[0-9a-f]{7,40}`), the step itself found the same 9 and reported them in its second MINOR -- but it put them in the RESOLVING bucket ('218 that resolve (209 after dropping 9 malformed non-sha strings)') when they resolve to nothing. Its own underlying resolving count of 209 matches mine exactly (211 today minus this run's 2). NOT MATERIALLY DIFFERENT FROM 57%: 58.1% vs 57% is 1.1 points on the same side of the same conclusion -- most recorded shas are dead -- so this is not a FAIL. Filed as MINOR 1 because a protocol document now quotes a checkable number that is nine shas wrong. One further trivium: of the 211 that resolve, 1 is a blob rather than a commit.

CHECK 2 -- MECHANISM. `GIT_MERGE.md` opened directly. Step 5 (line 71-72) is `5. Rebase onto origin/main: git rebase origin/main`; step 8 (line 209-211) is `8. Merge PR immediately ... gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`. Both say exactly what the subsection attributes to them. The mechanism explains the number: a rebase replays every branch commit under a new sha and a squash collapses the branch into one new commit on main and deletes the branch, so any sha an agent recorded mid-run is dead the moment its own run reaches step 5 or step 8 -- and since the protocol makes both mandatory, a MAJORITY of dead shas is the predicted outcome, not an anomaly. Corroboration re-run on main: `git log --oneline | grep -c '(#[0-9]*)'` = 175 squash commits, `git log --merges --oneline | wc -l` = 15 true merges; both match. WF02-REQ042 CHECKED INDEPENDENTLY: I read the run's own handoffs rather than the report -- step-02a records ['5b5dea4e1afa...', 'c1a4c2ecfcea...'], step-02c records ['5b5dea4'], step-03 records ['80f66a2']. `git cat-file -t` on all three: 'fatal: Not a valid object name' for every one. The work is on main as `84a0dab feat: Definition full-text search (store.zig's search, PD-10) [WF02-REQ042-20260817] (#123)`. The worked case is exactly as described, and is in fact stronger than reported -- all THREE of that run's recorded shas are dead, not just c1a4c2e.

CHECK 3 -- REGRESS REFUTATION, RE-DERIVED, AND IT HOLDS. `git log --oneline --all -- handoffs/` filtered on git_evidence|sha returns 23 commits. I classified each by whether its diff actually adds a quoted sha rather than by reading the subject: 2 are false positives and 21 are genuine, matching the step exactly. THE REPORTED FALSE POSITIVE IS REAL -- 25440db 'docs(ISS-0119): declare the three volume-1 shape anomalies' matches only on 'sha' inside 'shape' and adds no sha; the second, which the step counted but did not name, is 6c999e4 'design(ISS-0119): amend for three shape anomalies', same cause. TERMINATION CONFIRMED: all 21 touch exactly one handoff file each, and none records itself. I then took every sha in the whole corpus and tested each of the 21 write-back shas against it by prefix in both directions: ZERO hits. The regress the issue posits has never occurred and cannot, because no write-back is ever itself recorded. ORCH's filed premise was wrong and the subsection is right to say so. Concentration confirmed too: 11 run directories out of 63 on disk, 7 of the 21 in WF02-REQ049 alone. Two departures from the step's phrasing, neither touching the refutation, filed as MINOR 2: the count of run directories is 11, not 12; and 'every one records exactly its immediate predecessor' is true of 17 of 21 -- 426814c records its parent plus one earlier commit, and the three Step-Final commits d4e80ed, 09aaaef and f7dc7a2 record a post-merge squash sha (d4e80ed records 717208d, which is not its parent 419f1f2, at all). I also re-derived the subsection's 94-self-hits figure, which the dispatch did not ask for, by testing whether each resolving sha's commit touched the very file listing it: 94 of 211 -- EXACT MATCH.

CHECK 4 -- THE RULING, JUDGED ON ITS OWN TEXT. Read in full at HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:311-386. CRITERION 3 (the field keeps a stated purpose, is not decorative): MET. The text opens with 'What the field IS for' and gives it a job -- 'a convenience pointer to the commits this step produced, so a reader who has the handoff in front of them can reach the diff without reconstructing the run's history first' -- and then bounds it, 'It is not the audit trail', naming `git log --oneline -- handoffs/<run_id>/` as authoritative on disagreement. A reader is left with a reason to fill it and a reason not to over-trust it. CRITERION 1 (a reader can tell structural incompleteness from careless filling): MET, and concretely rather than by assertion. Three enumerated things the list cannot contain -- its own landing commit, anything recorded before the run's rebase, anything recorded before its squash-merge -- each tied to the protocol step that causes it. Then the two readings a reader actually needs: an empty list means this step committed nothing beyond its own handoff and 'never means the agent forgot'; a non-empty list means these were this step's commits at the moment of writing and 'never means all the commits of this run' and 'never means these still resolve'. And the decisive sentence for the criterion: 'A reader who hits an unresolvable sha has found a rebased or squashed branch, not a careless agent.' That is the discrimination the issue asked for, stated in the direction a reader will meet it.

CHECK 5 -- ONE CANONICAL STATEMENT AND THE SECTION 1.2 FENCE. `grep -rn commit_sha_list docs/ .claude/ --include=*.md` returns exactly one hit outside HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md: GIT_MERGE.md:215. That addition is six lines under step 8, states the invalidating mechanism in one sentence, adds the operational consequence ('do not go back and rewrite handoffs after the merge'), and ends 'HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2's commit_sha_list subsection is the canonical statement of what that field covers; this line does not restate it.' A POINTER, NOT A SECOND COPY -- it carries no part of the scope ruling, no measurement, and no empty/non-empty reading. Nothing was added to ORCHESTRATOR.md or core-directives.md. SECTION 1.2 UNTOUCHED, MECHANICALLY: `git show --numstat 12f8f4c` gives 77/0 on HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md -- insertions only, so no line in that file changed -- and the single hunk is at @@ -308. Section 1.2 spans lines 78-204 (`grep -n '^## '`). 389eb0b's 1/1 edit is at line 370. ISS-0206's and ISS-0208's subject matter was not taken.

CHECK 6 -- BOUNDARY AND NO-BACKFILL. `12f8f4c` exists (12f8f4cdce9c35a8775aa8b82cbe6bc02ebff045) and is the commit carrying the subsection: its diff adds the 77 lines to HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2, the 6-line GIT_MERGE.md pointer, and the ISS-0209.yaml resolution. NO BACKFILL: across all three commits the only handoff file touched is this run's own step-03 handoff, created new by 483726a at 78/0. Not one historical handoff appears in any of the three, and the 276 files that already carried a non-empty list are untouched -- confirmed both by the numstats and by the corpus walk, where the only non-empty-list change since the step's measurement is that one new file. 389eb0b DID ONLY THE ONE THING: 1 insertion, 1 deletion, one file, replacing the placeholder `SHA-PENDING-WRITEBACK` with `12f8f4c` in the boundary sentence and nothing else. It is itself a write-back that records only its immediate predecessor, is recorded nowhere, and the subsection's closing paragraph declares it -- consistent with the rule it just wrote.

CHECK 7 -- BOOKKEEPING. Both JSON files in this run's directory parse under json.loads. step-03's `result.status` is 'PASS', one of the legal five. `git diff --numstat`: handoffs/orchestrator.log 9/0 and handoffs/registry.json 20/0 -- ZERO DELETIONS on both, append-only clean. Neither was opened for edit by me; both remain uncommitted and ORCH's. `git status --porcelain` shows only those two modified plus this gate handoff untracked. No file outside docs/ and handoffs/WF03-ISS0209-20260821/ was modified by the run.

GATE DISPOSITION: PASS, and the run is releasable. The two MINORs below are defects in the artefact under review -- checkable numbers in a protocol document that do not match the repository -- not stylistic observations; neither changes the ruling, the direction chosen, or the refutation, and neither justifies rework on its own. Per the dispatch's scope paragraph I looked for and deliberately did not report wording, structure or adjacent-text observations; the verdict against the nine criteria is the deliverable.

issues.description: A checkable number now quoted in a protocol document is nine shas wrong. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2's new subsection states '284 - 57% - no longer resolve to any object in this repository' out of 502; ISS-0209.yaml's resolution and 12f8f4c's commit message repeat it. Re-derived: 293 of 502 were unresolvable at the step's own measurement moment (58.4%), and 293 of 504 are today (58.1%). The delta is not drift -- it is exactly the 9 non-sha-shaped strings the step itself found and reported in its own second MINOR, which it then counted in the resolving bucket ('218 that resolve (209 after dropping 9 malformed non-sha strings)') although they resolve to nothing; its underlying resolving count of 209 matches mine exactly. NOT MATERIAL and NOT A FAIL: same conclusion, same order of magnitude, 1.1 points. Fixing it is a three-figure edit in two files (284 -> 293, 57% -> 58%, and optionally 'of the 502, 9 are not sha-shaped at all') and is cheap to fold into whichever run next touches this subsection rather than a rework of this one.

Two write-back characterisations in the same subsection are slightly stronger than the history supports. (a) 'spanning 12 of the 63 run directories' -- it is 11, counted by the path of the file each of the 21 write-backs touches: WF03-ISS0204, WF03-ISS0201, WF03-ISS0198, WF03-ISS0119, ADHOC-20260821-002, WF02-REQ060, WF02-REQ049 (7 of the 21), WF03-ISS0043, WF03-ISS0029, WF02-REQ037, WF02-REQ036. The 21 and the 63 are both right. (b) 'every one records exactly its immediate predecessor and stops' holds for 17 of 21, not all: 426814c records its parent plus one earlier commit, and the three Step-Final commits d4e80ed, 09aaaef and f7dc7a2 record a post-merge squash sha -- d4e80ed records 717208d, which is not its parent 419f1f2 at all. THE REFUTATION IS UNAFFECTED, because it rests on the part I confirmed absolutely: none of the 21 records itself and none is recorded anywhere in the corpus, so there is no regress. The instruction that follows ('record only the commit before it, and do not record the write-back') is also unaffected. Worth ORCH's attention for a reason beyond accuracy: those three exceptions are already recording the durable post-merge squash sha, which is precisely what the step's own first MINOR proposes as the follow-on. That follow-on has prior art in this repository and the subsection currently describes it as a deviation.

result.next_action: ORCH: close the run. Gate is PASS; queue task 209 is releasable and no rework is owed. This gate wrote no docs and no code -- it is a gate, not a producer -- so commit_sha_list above is empty, which per the ruling just landed means exactly 'this step committed nothing beyond its own handoff file', not that anything was forgotten; the commit carrying this file is structurally absent from it and no write-back is owed. handoffs/registry.json (20/0) and handoffs/orchestrator.log (9/0) are still yours and still uncommitted; I did not touch either. File the two MINORs above if you want them fixed -- MINOR 1 is a three-figure correction to HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2 and ISS-0209.yaml, MINOR 2 is two clauses in the same subsection, and both are small enough to fold into the next run that touches this text rather than to carry a run each. If you also file the step-03 handoff's own first MINOR (recording the durable post-merge squash sha in the Step Final handoff), note that MINOR 2 found three commits already doing it, which is prior art that run can build on.
